sentences.zh: 李嗣業李嗣業，字嗣業，京兆高陵人。

translations.literal: Li Siye—Li Siye, courtesy name Siye, was a native of Gaoling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye, whose courtesy name was also Siye, came from Gaoling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 長七尺，膂力絕眾。

translations.literal: He was seven chi in height, and his arm strength surpassed the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi tall, and his physical strength surpassed all others.

sentences.zh: 開元中，從安西都護來曜討十姓蘇祿，先登捕虜，累功署昭武校尉。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, he followed the Protector-General of Anxi, Lai Yao, in attacking the Ten-Surname Sulu. He was first to ascend and capture enemies; for accumulated merit he was appointed Zhaowu Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, he followed Lai Yao, Protector-General of Anxi, in the campaign against the Ten-Surname Sulu. He was first over the walls and took prisoners; for repeated merit he was appointed Zhaowu Commandant.

sentences.zh: 後應募安西，軍中初用陌刀，而嗣業尤善，每戰必為先鋒，所向摧北。

translations.literal: Later he answered recruitment to Anxi. The army had just begun using the mo dao, and Siye was especially skilled. In every battle he necessarily served as vanguard; wherever he went the enemy was crushed and routed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he enlisted in Anxi. The army had only recently adopted the mo dao, and Siye excelled with it above all others. In every battle he led the vanguard, and wherever he went the enemy was shattered and driven back.

sentences.zh: 馬靈察為節度，出戰必與俱。

translations.literal: When Ma Lingcha became military commissioner, whenever he went out to battle he always went together with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Lingcha became military commissioner, Siye always accompanied him whenever he took the field.

sentences.zh: 高仙芝討勃律，署嗣業及中郎將田珍為左右陌刀將。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi attacked Baltistan and appointed Siye and the Palace Gentleman Tian Zhen as the left and right mo dao commanders.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Xianzhi campaigned against Baltistan, he appointed Siye and Tian Zhen, a palace gentleman, as commanders of the left and right mo dao units.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃兵十萬屯娑勒城，據山瀕水，聯木作郛，以扼王師。

translations.literal: At that time a hundred thousand Tibetan troops were encamped at Sale City. They held the mountains beside the water and linked timbers to make ramparts, to choke off the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time one hundred thousand Tibetan troops held Sale City. They occupied the heights above the water, linked timber into palisades, and blocked the imperial army's advance.

sentences.zh: 仙芝潛軍夜濟信圖河，令曰：「及午破賊，不者皆死。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi secretly moved the army by night across the Xintu River and issued the order: "By noon break the enemy—otherwise all shall die."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi secretly crossed the Xintu River by night and gave the order: "Break the enemy by noon, or you all die."

sentences.zh: 」嗣業提步士升山，頹石四面以擊賊，又樹大旗先走險，諸將從之。

translations.literal: Siye led foot soldiers up the mountain and toppled stones on all four sides to strike the enemy. He also planted a great banner and was first to take the hazardous path; the generals followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Siye led foot soldiers up the mountain and hurled boulders down on every side against the enemy. He raised a great banner and was first to take the dangerous route; the other generals followed.

sentences.zh: 虜不虞軍至，因大潰，投崖谷死者十八。

translations.literal: The enemy did not anticipate the army's arrival and so broke in great rout. Eight-tenths of those who plunged from cliffs and ravines died.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy did not expect the army's arrival and broke in complete rout. Eight out of ten who fell from cliffs and ravines died.

sentences.zh: 鼓而驅至勃律，禽其主，平之。

translations.literal: Beating drums, they drove to Baltistan, captured its ruler, and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Beating drums, they pressed on to Baltistan, captured its king, and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 授右威衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Weiwwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of the Right Weiwwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 從平石國及突騎施，以跳蕩先鋒加特進。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Kingdom of Shi and the Turgesh. For serving as a charging vanguard he received the honorary title Special Advance in Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying the Kingdom of Shi and the Turgesh, and for his service as a shock vanguard he was granted the honorary title Special Advance in Rank.

sentences.zh: 虜號為「神通大將」。

translations.literal: The enemy called him the "General of Supernatural Powers."
translations.idiomatic: The enemy called him the "General of Supernatural Powers."

sentences.zh: 初，仙芝特以計襲取石，其子出奔，因構諸胡共怨之，以告大食，連兵攻四鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gao Xianzhi had relied on a stratagem to seize the Kingdom of Shi by surprise. Its ruler's son fled, and he stirred the various foreign peoples to common resentment, reporting this to the Arabs. Allied forces then attacked the Four Garrisons in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Xianzhi had used a stratagem to seize the Kingdom of Shi by surprise. The king's son fled, and Gao stirred the various foreign peoples to shared resentment and reported the matter to the Arabs. Allied armies then attacked the Four Garrisons one after another.

sentences.zh: 仙芝率兵二萬深入，為大食所敗，殘卒數千。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi led twenty thousand troops in a deep advance and was defeated by the Arabs, leaving only a few thousand survivors.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi led twenty thousand men deep into enemy territory and was defeated by the Arabs, with only a few thousand survivors left.

sentences.zh: 事急，嗣業謀曰：「將軍深履賊境，後援既絕，而大食乘勝，諸胡銳於鬥，我與將軍俱前死，尚誰報朝廷者？

translations.literal: Matters grew urgent. Siye advised: "General, you have penetrated deep into enemy territory. Rear support is already cut off, the Arabs are riding their victory, and the various foreign peoples are keen to fight. If you and I both die here in the fore, who will still bear report to the court?"
translations.idiomatic: The situation turned desperate. Siye advised, "General, you have marched deep into enemy country. Our rear is cut off, the Arabs are pressing their advantage, and the foreign peoples are eager for battle. If you and I both die here at the front, who will carry word back to the court?"

sentences.zh: 不如守白石嶺以為後計。

translations.literal: Better to hold Bai shi Ridge as a plan for what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: We should hold Bai shi Ridge and plan from there.

sentences.zh: 」仙芝曰：「吾方收合餘盡，明日復戰。

translations.literal: Gao Xianzhi said: "I am just now gathering the remaining survivors—we will fight again tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianzhi said, "I am still gathering the survivors. We will fight again tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 」嗣業曰：「事去矣，不可坐須菹醢。

translations.literal: Siye said: "The chance is already lost. We cannot sit here waiting to be chopped up for mincemeat."
translations.idiomatic: Siye said, "The opportunity is gone. We cannot sit here waiting to be butchered."

sentences.zh: 」即馳守白石，路既隘，步騎魚貫而前。

translations.literal: At once he rode to hold Bai shi. The road was narrow, and foot and horse passed through in single file.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately rode to hold Bai shi Ridge. The road was narrow, and infantry and cavalry filed through in single column.

sentences.zh: 會拔汗那還兵，輜餉塞道不可騁，嗣業懼追及，手梃鏖擊，人馬斃僕者數十百，虜駭走，仙芝乃得還。

translations.literal: They happened to meet the returning troops of Ferghana. Baggage carts choked the road and cavalry could not gallop free. Siye, fearing pursuit, fought hand-to-hand with a cudgel. Dozens upon hundreds of men and horses were struck down and fell; the enemy fled in alarm, and only then could Gao Xianzhi get back.
translations.idiomatic: They met the returning army of Ferghana. Supply wagons blocked the road so cavalry could not ride freely. Fearing pursuit, Siye fought hand to hand with a club, killing dozens or even hundreds of men and horses. The enemy fled in terror, and only then was Gao Xianzhi able to escape.

sentences.zh: 表嗣業功，進右金吾大將軍，留為疏勒鎮使。

translations.literal: They memorialized Siye's merit. He was promoted to Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard and retained as military commissioner at Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: Siye's achievements were reported to the throne. He was promoted to Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guard and kept on as military commissioner at Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 城一隅阤，屢築輒壞，嗣業祝之，有白龍見，因其處蕝祠以祭，城遂不壞，漢耿恭故井久涸，禱已，泉復出。

translations.literal: One corner of the city wall kept collapsing however often they rebuilt it. Siye prayed over it, and a white dragon appeared. He built a mound-shrine on that spot and offered sacrifice; the wall then held firm. An old well from Han times associated with Geng Gong had long run dry; after prayer the spring flowed again.
translations.idiomatic: One section of the city wall repeatedly collapsed no matter how often it was rebuilt. Siye prayed over it, and a white dragon appeared. He built a mound-shrine on that spot and made offerings, and the wall stood firm thereafter. An ancient well associated with Geng Gong of Han had long been dry; after his prayers the spring flowed again.

sentences.zh: 初討勃律也，通道蔥領，有大石塞隘，以足蹶之，抵穹壑，識者以為至誠所感雲。

translations.literal: When they first attacked Baltistan, they opened a route over the Congling passes. A great boulder blocked the narrows. He kicked it with his foot and it rolled into a deep ravine. Those who understood such things took it as a sign moved by utmost sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: During the first campaign against Baltistan, they opened a route through the Congling passes. A huge boulder blocked the narrow way. Siye kicked it with his foot and sent it tumbling into a deep gorge. Observers believed this was a response to his utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 天寶十二載，加驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Tianbao he was additionally made General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Tianbao he was further promoted to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 入朝，賜酒玄宗前，醉起舞，帝寵之，賜彩百、金皿五十物、錢十萬，曰：「為解酲具。

translations.literal: He entered court. Wine was granted before Emperor Xuanzong. Drunk, he rose to dance. The Emperor favored him and bestowed a hundred rolls of silk, fifty gold vessels, and a hundred thousand coins, saying: "These are to restore you from drunkenness."
translations.idiomatic: He came to court and was given wine in Emperor Xuanzong's presence. Drunk, he rose and danced. The Emperor was delighted and granted him a hundred rolls of silk, fifty gold vessels, and a hundred thousand coins, saying, "These are to sober you up."

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，肅宗追之，詔至，即引道，與諸將割臂盟曰：「所過郡縣，秋毫不可犯。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Emperor Suzong pursued him. When the edict arrived, Siye at once set out on the road. With the generals he cut their arms and swore an oath, saying: "In every commandery and county we pass through, not even the slightest thing may be violated."
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Emperor Suzong marched against him. As soon as the edict arrived, Siye set out at once. He and the other generals cut their arms and swore an oath: "In every commandery and county we pass through, not the slightest thing shall be harmed."

sentences.zh: 」至鳳翔，上謁，帝喜曰：「今日卿至，賢於數萬眾。

translations.literal: At Fengxiang he had an audience with the Emperor, who said in delight: "Your arrival today is worth more than tens of thousands of troops."
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang he had an audience with the Emperor, who said with delight, "Your arrival today is worth more than an army of tens of thousands."

sentences.zh: 事之濟否，固在卿輩。

translations.literal: Whether this enterprise succeeds or fails indeed rests with you.
translations.idiomatic: Whether this undertaking succeeds or fails depends entirely on you.

sentences.zh: 」乃詔與郭子儀、僕固懷恩掎角。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued ordering him to coordinate pincer movements with Guo Ziyi and Pugu Huai'en.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered him to coordinate pincer attacks with Guo Ziyi and Pugu Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 常為先鋒，以巨棓笞鬥，賊值，類崩潰。

translations.literal: He constantly served as vanguard, beating the enemy with great cudgels. When the rebels encountered him they invariably collapsed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He always led the vanguard, striking the enemy with great clubs. Whenever the rebels met him they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 進四鎮、伊西、北庭行軍兵馬使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Four Garrisons, Yixi, and Beiting Marching Armies and Horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Marching Armies and Horses of the Four Garrisons, Yixi, and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 廣平王收長安，嗣業統前軍，陣於香積祠北。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Guangping recovered Chang'an, Siye commanded the vanguard and formed battle lines north of the Xiangji Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Guangping recaptured Chang'an, Siye commanded the advance force and drew up battle lines north of the Xiangji Shrine.

sentences.zh: 賊酋李歸仁擁精騎薄戰，王師注矢逐之，走未及營，賊大出，掩追騎，還蹂王師，於是亂不能陣。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain Li Guiren led picked cavalry to press the attack. The imperial army strung bows and chased them. Before the rebels reached their camp, the main rebel force poured out, enveloped the pursuing cavalry, wheeled back to trample the imperial army, and the ranks fell into disorder and could no longer hold formation.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chieftain Li Guiren led elite cavalry in a close assault. The imperial army strung their bows and pursued. Before the rebels reached their camp, the main rebel force surged out, cut off the pursuing cavalry, and wheeled back to trample the imperial lines. The army fell into chaos and could no longer hold formation.

sentences.zh: 嗣業謂子儀曰：「今日不蹈萬死取一生，則軍無類矣。

translations.literal: Siye said to Guo Ziyi: "Today, unless we tread through ten thousand deaths to win one life, the army will not survive."
translations.idiomatic: Siye said to Guo Ziyi, "Today, unless we risk death ten thousand times to win a single chance at life, this army will be wiped out."

sentences.zh: 」即袒持長刀，大呼出陣前，殺數十人，陣復整。

translations.literal: Barechested he seized a long blade, shouted, and charged out before the battle line. He killed several dozen men, and the formation regained order.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped to the waist, seized a long blade, shouted, and charged out before the lines. He killed several dozen men, and the formation steadied again.

sentences.zh: 步卒二千以陌刀、長柯斧堵進，所向無前。

translations.literal: Two thousand foot soldiers advanced in a wall formation with mo dao and long-shafted axes; wherever they went nothing stood before them.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand foot soldiers advanced in a solid wall with mo dao and long-shafted axes. Nothing could stand before them.

sentences.zh: 歸仁匿兵營左，覘軍勢，王分回紇銳兵擊其伏，嗣業出賊背合攻之，自日中至昃，斬首六萬級，填澗壑死幾半，賊東走，遂平長安。

translations.literal: Li Guiren hid troops to the left of the camp to watch the army's movements. The Prince sent elite Uyghur troops to strike the ambush. Siye emerged behind the enemy and attacked together with them. From midday until the late afternoon they took sixty thousand heads; nearly half the dead filled ravines and gullies. The rebels fled east, and Chang'an was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guiren hid troops to the left of the camp to observe the imperial army. The Prince sent elite Uyghur cavalry against the ambush while Siye struck from behind the enemy. From midday until late afternoon they took sixty thousand heads; nearly half the dead filled ravines and gullies. The rebels fled east, and Chang'an was recovered.

sentences.zh: 進收東都，嗣業戰多。

translations.literal: They advanced to recover the Eastern Capital. Siye fought in many engagements.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to recover the Eastern Capital, and Siye fought in many battles.

sentences.zh: 乃與張鎬、魯炅、來瑱、嗣吳王祗、李奐略定諸州。

translations.literal: He then joined Zhang Gao, Lu Kui, Lai Tian, the Heir Prince Wu Wang Zhi, and Li Huan in subduing and settling the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Zhang Gao, Lu Kui, Lai Tian, the Heir Prince of Wu, Li Zhi, and Li Huan in pacifying the various provinces.

sentences.zh: 兼衛尉卿，封虢國公，實封戶二百。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Guo, and received two hundred taxable households as a fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was also appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, enfeoffed as Duke of Guo, and granted two hundred taxable households as a fief.

sentences.zh: 兼懷州刺史、北庭行營節度使。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as Prefect of Huaizhou and military commissioner of the Beiting field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Prefect of Huaizhou and military commissioner of the Beiting field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 與子儀等圍相州，師耄，諸將無功，獨嗣業被堅數奮，為諸軍冠。

translations.literal: With Guo Ziyi and the others he besieged Xiangzhou. The army was worn out, and the generals achieved nothing. Only Siye, clad in heavy armor, repeatedly took the lead in fierce charges and stood at the head of all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: With Guo Ziyi and the others he besieged Xiangzhou. The army had grown exhausted, and the other generals achieved nothing. Only Siye, in heavy armor, repeatedly charged with fierce valor and led all the armies.

sentences.zh: 中流矢，臥帳中，方愈，忽聞金鼓聲，知與賊戰，大呼，創潰，血流數升卒。

translations.literal: He was struck by an arrow and lay in his tent convalescing. Just as he was recovering, he suddenly heard drums and gongs and knew the army was fighting the rebels. He gave a great shout; his wound burst open and blood poured out by the sheng—he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck by an arrow and lay convalescing in his tent. Just as he was recovering, he suddenly heard drums and gongs and knew the army was fighting the rebels. He shouted loudly; his wound burst open, blood poured out by the sheng, and he died.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠勇，贈武威郡王，給靈輿護還在所。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Loyal and Brave. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei Commandery, and an imperial catafalque was provided to escort his body home.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Loyal and Brave, posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei Commandery, and granted an imperial catafalque to escort his body home.

sentences.zh: 葬日，使中人臨吊，中朝臣祖泣，塋給掃除十戶。

translations.literal: On the day of burial, palace eunuchs were sent to attend the mourning. Court ministers wept in farewell. Ten households were assigned to maintain his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his burial, palace eunuchs were sent to offer condolences. Court ministers wept as they saw him off. Ten households were assigned to maintain his tomb.

sentences.zh: 嗣業忠毅憂國，不計居產，有宛馬十疋，前後賞賜，皆上於官以助軍雲。

translations.literal: Siye was loyal, resolute, and concerned for the state. He gave no thought to personal property. He possessed ten Ferghana horses, and all rewards granted him before and after he turned over to the government to aid the army—or so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Siye was loyal, resolute, and devoted to the state. He cared nothing for personal wealth. He owned ten Ferghana horses, and all the rewards he received, before and after, he turned over to the government to support the army—or so it is said.

sentences.zh: 子佐國，襲爵，曆丹王府長史。

translations.literal: His son Zuoguo inherited the title and served as Chief Administrator of the Prince of Dan's household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuoguo inherited the title and served as chief administrator of the Prince of Dan's household.

sentences.zh: 卒，推嗣業功，贈宋州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died, in recognition of Siye's merit he was posthumously made Prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuoguo died, in recognition of Siye's achievements he was posthumously appointed Prefect of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 馬璘馬璘，岐州扶風人。

translations.literal: Ma Lin—Ma Lin was a native of Fufeng in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin came from Fufeng in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，流蕩無業所。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he drifted about with no settled occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he wandered without a settled livelihood.

sentences.zh: 年二十，讀漢馬援傳，至「丈夫當死邊野，以馬革裹屍而歸」，慨然曰：「使吾祖勳業墜於地乎？

translations.literal: At age twenty, reading the Han biography of Ma Yuan, he came to the passage "A true man should die on the frontier wilds and return wrapped in horsehide." He sighed deeply and said: "Shall my forebear's achievements fall to the ground?"
translations.idiomatic: At twenty, reading the Han biography of Ma Yuan, he came to the line, "A true man should die on the frontier wilds and return wrapped in horsehide." He sighed and said, "Shall my ancestor's achievements be lost to the ground?"

sentences.zh: 」開元末，挾策從安西節度府，以奇勞，累遷金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he took up arms and joined the Anxi military commissioner's staff. For extraordinary service he was repeatedly promoted, eventually reaching General of the Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan reign he took up arms and joined the staff of the Anxi military commissioner. For distinguished service he rose through the ranks until he became General of the Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 至德初，王室多難，統精甲三千，自二庭赴鳳翔。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era, when the royal house faced many troubles, he led three thousand picked armored troops from the Two Courts to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Zhide reign, when the dynasty was in crisis, he led three thousand elite armored troops from Beiting and Tingzhou to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 肅宗奇之，委以東討。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong was impressed and entrusted him with the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was impressed and entrusted him with the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 初戰衛南，以百騎破賊五千眾。

translations.literal: In his first battle at Weinan he broke five thousand rebels with a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: In his first battle at Weinan he routed five thousand rebels with only a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 從李光弼攻洛陽，史朝義眾十萬陣北邙山，旗鎧照日，諸疑，未敢擊。

translations.literal: Following Li Guangbi in the attack on Luoyang, he faced Shi Chaoyi's force of a hundred thousand arrayed on Mount Beimang; banners and armor blazed in the sun. The other commanders hesitated and dared not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Following Li Guangbi in the attack on Luoyang, he found Shi Chaoyi's army of one hundred thousand drawn up on Mount Beimang, banners and armor blazing in the sun. The other commanders hesitated and dared not attack.

sentences.zh: 璘率部士五百，薄賊屯，出入三反，眾披靡，乘之，賊遂潰。

translations.literal: Ma Lin led five hundred of his men and pressed close to the enemy camp. Three times he charged in and out; the mass broke and scattered. Pressing the advantage, he put the rebels to rout.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin led five hundred of his men in a close assault on the enemy camp. Three times he charged in and out until the enemy ranks collapsed. Pressing the advantage, he put the rebels to flight.

sentences.zh: 光弼曰：「吾用兵三十年，未見以少擊眾，雄捷如馬將軍者！

translations.literal: Li Guangbi said: "In thirty years of commanding armies I have never seen one who fights few against many with such fierce agility as General Ma!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi said, "In thirty years of commanding armies I have never seen anyone fight so few against so many with such fierce speed as General Ma!"

sentences.zh: 」遷試太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred and given provisional appointment as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred and given provisional appointment as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 明年，吐蕃寇邊，詔璘移軍援河西。

translations.literal: The next year the Tibetans raided the frontier. An edict ordered Ma Lin to move his army to reinforce Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Tibetans raided the frontier, and an edict ordered Ma Lin to move his army to reinforce Hexi.

sentences.zh: 懷恩之叛，璘引還，間關轉鬥至鳳翔，虜圍已合，節度使孫志直嬰城守。

translations.literal: When Huai'en rebelled, Ma Lin led his troops back. Fighting through peril after peril he reached Fengxiang. The enemy siege was already closed; the military commissioner Sun Zhizhi held the city under siege defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, Ma Lin led his troops back. Fighting through one danger after another he reached Fengxiang, where the enemy siege was already complete and Military Commissioner Sun Zhizhi was holding the city.

sentences.zh: 璘令士持滿外向，突入縣門，不解甲出戰，背城陣。

translations.literal: Ma Lin ordered his men to hold their bows fully drawn facing outward. They burst through the county gate, went to battle without removing their armor, and formed lines with their backs to the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin ordered his men to hold their bows at full draw facing outward. They burst through the county gate, fought without removing their armor, and formed battle lines with their backs to the city wall.

sentences.zh: 虜潰，率輕騎追之，斬數千級，漂血丹渠。

translations.literal: The enemy broke and fled. Leading light cavalry in pursuit he took several thousand heads; blood stained the Dan Canal red.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy broke and fled. Leading light cavalry in pursuit, he took several thousand heads, and blood dyed the Dan Canal red.

sentences.zh: 帝引見尉勞，擢兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned him for an audience and consoled him with rewards, promoting him to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received him in audience, rewarded him, and promoted him to concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，拜四鎮行營節度、南道和蕃使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yongtai era he was appointed military commissioner of the Four Garrisons field headquarters and commissioner for pacifying the Tibetans on the Southern Route.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yongtai reign he was appointed military commissioner of the Four Garrisons field headquarters and commissioner for relations with the Tibetans on the Southern Route.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校工部尚書，北庭行營、邠甯節度使。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Beiting field headquarters and Binning circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Beiting field headquarters and Binning circuit.

sentences.zh: 元日，有卒犯盜，或曰宜赦，璘曰：「赦之，則人將伺其日為盜。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day a soldier committed theft. Some said he should be pardoned. Ma Lin said: "If he is pardoned, people will watch for that day to steal."
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day a soldier committed theft. Some suggested he should be pardoned. Ma Lin said, "If we pardon him, people will mark that day for stealing."

sentences.zh: 」遂戮之。

translations.literal: He had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: He had the man executed.

sentences.zh: 天大旱，裏巷為土龍聚巫以禱，璘曰：「旱由政不修。

translations.literal: There was severe drought. Lanes and alleys raised earthen dragons and gathered shamans to pray. Ma Lin said: "Drought comes because government is not properly maintained."
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought struck. People in the lanes and alleys built earthen dragons and gathered shamans to pray for rain. Ma Lin said, "Drought comes from failure to govern well."

sentences.zh: 」即命撤之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered them dismantled.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered them torn down.

sentences.zh: 明日雨，是歲大穰。

translations.literal: The next day rain fell, and that year brought a great harvest.
translations.idiomatic: The next day it rained, and that year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙涇原，權知鳳翔、隴右節度副使，四鎮、北庭如舊，復以鄭、潁二州隸之。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Jingyuan, given provisional charge as deputy military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou, with the Four Garrisons and Beiting as before, and the two prefectures of Zheng and Ying were again placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Jingyuan and given provisional charge as deputy military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou, with the Four Garrisons and Beiting unchanged. The prefectures of Zheng and Ying were again placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，吐蕃內寇，渾瑊戰宜祿，不利。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali the Tibetans invaded the interior. Hun Zhen fought them at Yilu with unfavorable results.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dali the Tibetans invaded the interior. Hun Zhen fought them at Yilu with poor results.

sentences.zh: 璘設伏潘原，與瑊合擊破之，俘級數萬。

translations.literal: Ma Lin set an ambush at Panyuan and, joining with Hun Zhen, struck and defeated them, taking tens of thousands of captives and heads.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin set an ambush at Panyuan and, joining Hun Zhen, defeated them, taking tens of thousands of captives and heads.

sentences.zh: 進檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，入朝，求宰相，以檢校左僕射知省事，進撫風郡王。

translations.literal: The next year he entered court, sought the post of chief minister, was made acting Left Vice Director with charge of court business, and was advanced to Prince of Fufeng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court seeking the post of chief minister. He was made acting Left Vice Director with charge of court affairs and advanced to Prince of Fufeng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒於軍，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died in camp at age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died in camp at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈司徒，諡曰武。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Education, with the posthumous title Martial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Education and given the posthumous title Martial.

sentences.zh: 璘少學術，而武幹絕倫。

translations.literal: Ma Lin had studied the classics in youth, yet his martial prowess was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin had studied the classics in his youth, yet his martial prowess was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 遭時屯棘，以忠力奮。

translations.literal: He met a time of thorns and hardship and rose up through loyalty and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a time of hardship and rose through loyalty and force of arms.

sentences.zh: 在涇八年，繕屯壁，為戰守具，令肅不殘，人樂為用，虜不敢犯，為中興銳將。

translations.literal: During eight years at Jingzhou he repaired fortified camps and prepared equipment for attack and defense. His orders were strict but not cruel. Men were glad to serve him; the enemy dared not invade. He was a foremost general of the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: During eight years at Jingyuan he repaired fortified camps and prepared equipment for attack and defense. His orders were strict but not oppressive. His men served him gladly, and the enemy dared not attack. He was one of the great generals of the restoration.

sentences.zh: 初，涇軍乏財，帝諷李抱玉讓鄭、潁，璘因得裒積，且前後賜賚無算，家富不貲。

translations.literal: Initially the Jing army lacked funds. The Emperor hinted that Li Baoyu should yield Zheng and Ying, and so Ma Lin was able to accumulate wealth. Moreover, rewards granted him before and after were beyond counting; his household grew rich beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Jing army lacked funds. The Emperor hinted that Li Baoyu should yield Zheng and Ying, allowing Ma Lin to amass wealth. Rewards from before and after were beyond counting, and his household grew fabulously rich.

sentences.zh: 治第京師，侈甚，其寢堂無慮費錢二十萬緡。

translations.literal: He built a mansion in the capital, extravagantly splendid. His sleeping hall alone cost no less than two hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mansion in the capital of extravagant splendor. His sleeping hall alone cost no less than two hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 方璘在軍，守者覆以油幔。

translations.literal: While Ma Lin was still in the army, those guarding it covered the mansion with oiled curtains.
translations.idiomatic: While Ma Lin was still in the field, those guarding the mansion covered it with oiled curtains.

sentences.zh: 及喪歸，都人爭入觀，假稱故吏入赴吊者日數百。

translations.literal: When his funeral bier returned, capital residents scrambled to enter and view it. Those falsely claiming to be former subordinates coming to mourn numbered hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: When his funeral procession returned to the capital, residents scrambled to enter and view the mansion. Hundreds each day falsely claimed to be former subordinates coming to mourn.

sentences.zh: 德宗在東宮聞之，不喜。

translations.literal: When Dezong was still Crown Prince he heard of this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was still Crown Prince, he heard of this and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及即位，乃禁第捨不得逾制，詔毀璘中寢及宦人劉忠翼第。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, he forbade mansions to exceed prescribed standards and ordered the destruction of Ma Lin's central sleeping hall and the mansion of the eunuch Liu Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, he forbade mansions to exceed prescribed standards and ordered the destruction of Ma Lin's central sleeping hall and the mansion of the eunuch Liu Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 璘家懼，悉籍亭館入之官。

translations.literal: Ma Lin's family feared this and registered all pavilions and halls, surrendering them to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin's family, fearing further action, registered all pavilions and halls and surrendered them to the state.

sentences.zh: 其後賜群臣宴，多在璘山池。

translations.literal: Thereafter when the Emperor granted banquets to the ministers, he often held them at Ma Lin's hills and ponds.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when the Emperor gave banquets to his ministers, he often held them at Ma Lin's hills and ponds.

sentences.zh: 而子弟無行，財亦尋盡。

translations.literal: But his sons and younger relatives behaved without propriety, and the wealth was soon exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: But his sons and younger kinsmen behaved badly, and the fortune was soon spent.

sentences.zh: 李抱玉李抱玉，本安興貴曾孫，世居河西，善養馬。

translations.literal: Li Baoyu—Li Baoyu was originally a great-grandson of An Xinggui. His family had long lived in Hexi and was skilled at raising horses.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baoyu was originally a great-grandson of An Xinggui. His family had long lived in Hexi and was skilled at raising horses.

sentences.zh: 始名重璋，閑騎射，少從軍。

translations.literal: His original name was Chongzhang. He was adept at riding and archery and entered the army young.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Chongzhang. He was skilled in riding and archery and joined the army at a young age.

sentences.zh: 其為人沈毅有謀，尤忠謹，李光弼引為裨校。

translations.literal: As a man he was deep, resolute, and full of stratagem, and especially loyal and careful. Li Guangbi recruited him as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was deep, resolute, and resourceful, and especially loyal and careful. Li Guangbi took him on as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，玄宗以其戰河西有功，為改今名。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao, Emperor Xuanzong, because of his merit fighting in Hexi, changed his name to the present one.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao reign, Emperor Xuanzong changed his name to the present one in recognition of his achievements fighting in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，守南陽，斬賊使。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he defended Nanyang and beheaded the rebel envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, he defended Nanyang and beheaded the rebel envoy.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，上言：「世占涼州，恥與逆臣共宗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he submitted a memorial: "My family has held Liangzhou for generations. I am ashamed to share a surname with the rebel minister."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhide he submitted a memorial: "My family has held Liangzhou for generations. I am ashamed to share a surname with the rebel minister."

sentences.zh: 」有詔賜之姓，因徙籍京兆，舉族以李為氏。

translations.literal: An edict granted him the imperial surname. He therefore transferred his household registration to Jingzhao, and the whole clan took Li as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him the imperial surname. He transferred his household registration to Jingzhao, and the entire clan took Li as their surname.

sentences.zh: 進至右羽林大將軍，知軍事，擢陳鄭潁亳節度使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Right Feathered Forest Guards with command of military affairs and was elevated to Military Governor of Chen, Zheng, Ying, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General of the Right Feathered Forest Guards with command of military affairs and was appointed Military Governor of Chen, Zheng, Ying, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 史思明已破東都，兇焰勃然，鼓而行，自謂無前。

translations.literal: Shi Siming had already captured the Eastern Capital. His vicious flame blazed high. Beating drums, he marched, deeming himself unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming had already taken the Eastern Capital. His ferocity swelled; beating drums, he marched forward, certain none could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 光弼壁河陽拒之，使抱玉守南城。

translations.literal: Guangbi fortified at Heyang to resist him and had Baoyu defend the southern city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi fortified at Heyang to hold him back and set Baoyu to guard the southern city.

sentences.zh: 賊急攻，抱玉縱奇兵出，表裏俘殺甚眾。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked fiercely. Baoyu released surprise troops. Inside and outside they captured and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels pressed the attack, Baoyu sent elite troops out in a surprise maneuver, killing and capturing great numbers from within and without.

sentences.zh: 賊乃舍去，從光弼戰，大敗，因不能西。

translations.literal: The rebels then abandoned the siege, followed Guangbi to battle, suffered great defeat, and therefore could not advance west.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then withdrew, fought Li Guangbi, and were routed, so they could not push westward.

sentences.zh: 差功第一，封欒城縣公。

translations.literal: His merit was ranked first. He was enfeoffed as Duke of Luancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He was credited with the highest merit and enfeoffed as Duke of Luancheng County.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，兼澤潞節度使，統相、衛、儀、邢十一州兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong ascended, he additionally served as Military Governor of Ze and Lu, commanding the troops of eleven prefectures including Xiang, Wei, Yi, and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong came to the throne, Baoyu was also made Military Governor of Ze and Lu, commanding troops from eleven prefectures including Xiang, Wei, Yi, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 以功授司空，兼兵部尚書，武威郡王。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed Grand Master of Works, concurrently Minister of War, and Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was made Grand Master of Works, concurrently Minister of War, and Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 懇辭王爵，徙涼國公，進司徒。

translations.literal: He earnestly declined the princely rank, was transferred to Duke of Liang, and was promoted to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly declined the princely title and was made Duke of Liang instead, then promoted to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，吐蕃入寇，帝次陝，群盜遍南山五穀間，東距虢，西抵岐，椎剽不勝計。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era, the Tibetans invaded. The Emperor halted at Shan. Bandits spread throughout the valleys of the Southern Mountains, east from Guo to west reaching Qi. Robbery with clubs was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangde reign, when the Tibetans invaded and the Emperor halted at Shan, bandits filled the valleys of the Southern Mountains—from Guo in the east to Qi in the west—and pillaging was beyond count.

sentences.zh: 詔太子賓客薛景仙為南山五溪穀防禦使，引兵招捕，久不克。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Crown Prince Advisor Xue Jingxian as Defense Commissioner for the Five Streams and Valleys of the Southern Mountains, to lead troops in recruitment and capture. For a long time he could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Crown Prince Advisor Xue Jingxian Commissioner for the Defense of the Five Streams and Valleys of the Southern Mountains and sent him to lead troops against the bandits, but he could not suppress them for a long time.

sentences.zh: 更詔抱玉討賊。

translations.literal: The edict was changed to have Baoyu attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Baoyu to suppress the bandits.

sentences.zh: 抱玉盡得賊株柢蹊隧，分兵守諸穀，使牙將李崇客精騎四百，自桃林、虢川襲之。

translations.literal: Baoyu fully traced the bandits' roots, stalks, paths, and tunnels. He divided troops to guard the various valleys and sent his adjutant Li Chongke with four hundred elite horsemen to strike them from Taolin and Guochuan.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu traced the bandits' entire network of hideouts and secret routes, posted troops to guard the valleys, and sent his adjutant Li Chongke with four hundred elite cavalry to strike from Taolin and Guochuan.

sentences.zh: 賊帥高玉脫身走城固，山南西道張獻誠禽以獻，悉索支黨斬之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Gao Yu escaped and fled to Chenggu. Zhang Xiancheng of Shannan West Circuit captured him and presented him. All associates were sought out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Gao Yu fled to Chenggu, where Zhang Xiancheng of Shannan West Circuit captured and delivered him; all his followers were hunted down and executed.

sentences.zh: 不閱旬，五穀平。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days, the five valleys were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In less than ten days the five valleys were pacified.

sentences.zh: 即詔抱玉權鳳翔、隴右節度，抱玉懇讓司徒，故以尚書左僕射同中書門下平章事，河西、隴右副元帥。

translations.literal: Immediately Baoyu was ordered to act as Military Governor of Fengxiang and Longyou. Baoyu earnestly declined the post of Grand Preceptor, so he was given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Chief Councillor of the State Chancellery, and Vice Commander-in-Chief of Hexi and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu was promptly entrusted with the military governorships of Fengxiang and Longyou. He earnestly declined the Grand Preceptorship, so he was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Chief Councillor, and Vice Commander-in-Chief of Hexi and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 又讓僕射，故還為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He again declined the Vice Directorship, so he returned to the post of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the vice directorship as well and was restored to his post as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 大曆二年，來朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali, he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dali reign he came to court.

sentences.zh: 久之，加山南西道副元帥兼節度使，屯鷫厔。

translations.literal: After some time, he was additionally made Vice Commander-in-Chief and Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit, stationing at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was also made Vice Commander-in-Chief and Military Governor of Shannan West Circuit, with his headquarters at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 抱玉兼三節度、三副元帥，位望隆赫。

translations.literal: Baoyu concurrently held three military governorships and three vice commander posts. His position and prestige were lofty and brilliant.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu held three military governorships and three vice commanderships at once; his rank and prestige were immense.

sentences.zh: 乃上言：「隴坻達扶、文，綿地二千里，虜孔道不一，梁、岷重則關輔輕。

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial: "Longqi extends to Fu and Wen, a stretch of two thousand li. Enemy routes are not one. If Liang and Min are stressed, then Guanfu is slighted."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "From Longqi to Fu and Wen the territory runs two thousand li, with enemy access routes in many places. If we overweight Liang and Min, Guanfu will be neglected."

sentences.zh: 願擇能臣，帥西道當一面，臣得專事關、隴。

translations.literal: "I wish to select a capable minister to command the western circuit on one front, so that I may devote myself exclusively to Guan and Long."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask that a capable minister be chosen to hold the western front alone, so that I may devote myself entirely to Guan and Long."

sentences.zh: 」帝多其讓，許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired his yielding and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his humility and agreed.

sentences.zh: 抱玉在鎮十餘年，雖無破虜功，而禁暴安人，為將臣之良。

translations.literal: Baoyu was at his post for more than ten years. Though he had no merit in defeating barbarians, he forbade violence and settled the people, and was a fine general-minister.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu held his command for more than ten years. He won no great victories over invaders, but he suppressed violence and settled the populace—among generals and ministers he was exemplary.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四，贈太保，諡曰昭武。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-four. Posthumously he was given Grand Preceptor. His posthumous title was Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four. The court posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 從父弟 抱真從父弟抱真。

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Baozhen. Paternal cousin Baozhen.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin was Li Baozhen.

sentences.zh: 抱真字太玄，沈慮而斷。

translations.literal: Baozhen, courtesy name Taixuan, was deep in deliberation and decisive.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen, courtesy name Taixuan, was thoughtful and resolute.

sentences.zh: 抱玉屬以軍事，授汾州別駕。

translations.literal: Baoyu entrusted him with military affairs and appointed him Vice Prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu put him in charge of military affairs and appointed him Vice Prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩反，陷焉，挺身歸京師。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en rebelled and Fen fell. He went through bodily and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled and Fenzhou fell, he made his way alone back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗以懷恩倚回紇，所將朔方兵精，憂之，召抱真問狀，答曰：「郭子儀嘗領朔方軍，人多德之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong, because Huai'en relied on the Uyghurs and the Shuofang troops he led were elite, was worried. He summoned Baozhen to ask the situation. Baozhen replied: "Guo Ziyi once led the Shuofang army. Many men are grateful to him."
translations.idiomatic: Daizong worried because Huai'en relied on the Uyghurs and commanded the elite Shuofang army. He summoned Baozhen and asked his view. Baozhen answered: "Guo Ziyi once led the Shuofang army, and the men deeply revere him."

sentences.zh: 懷恩欺其下曰，'子儀為朝恩所殺。

translations.literal: Huai'en deceived his subordinates, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by Yu Chao'en on the emperor's orders.'
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en lied to his troops, saying, 'Guo Ziyi was murdered by Yu Chao'en on the emperor's orders.'

sentences.zh: '今起而用，是伐其謀，兵可不戰解也。

translations.literal: Now if we raise and employ him, this will cut down their plot. The troops can be dissolved without battle."
translations.idiomatic: If we recall and employ him now, we will destroy their scheme and the army can be disbanded without a fight."

sentences.zh: 」既而懷恩敗，如抱真策。

translations.literal: Soon after Huai'en was defeated, just as Baozhen had strategized.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was soon defeated, just as Baozhen had predicted.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中少監、陳鄭澤潞節度留後。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Administration and Acting Military Governor of Chen, Zheng, Ze, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Administration and made acting military governor of Chen, Zheng, Ze, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 既謝，因言：「百姓勞逸在牧守，願得一州以自試。

translations.literal: Having thanked the emperor, he then said: "The toil and ease of the common people depend on the prefects and governors. I wish to receive one prefecture to try myself."
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the appointment, he said: "Whether the people toil or rest depends on their local governors. I wish to be given one prefecture to prove myself."

sentences.zh: 」更授澤州刺史，兼澤潞節度副使。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Prefect of Zezhou, concurrently Vice Military Governor of Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Prefect of Zezhou and Vice Military Governor of Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 徙懷州，仍為懷澤潞觀察留後，凡八年。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Huai Prefecture, still serving as Acting Observation Commissioner of Huai, Ze, and Lu, for eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Huai Prefecture and continued as acting observation commissioner for Huai, Ze, and Lu—a post he held for eight years.

sentences.zh: 抱真策山東有變，澤、潞兵所走集，乘戰伐後，賦重人困，軍伍雕刓，乃籍戶三丁擇一，蠲其徭租，給弓矢，令閑月得曹偶習射，歲終大校，親按籍第能否賞責。

translations.literal: Baozhen judged that there would be upheaval in Shandong. Ze and Lu were where troops converged. Riding on the aftermath of warfare, taxes were heavy and the people were distressed; military ranks were cut down and depleted. Thereupon he registered households—one man chosen from every three—and exempted them from corvée and rent, supplied bows and arrows, ordered that in idle months they could gather in groups to practice archery. At year's end there was a great inspection; he personally went through the registers and graded ability, rewarding and punishing.
translations.idiomatic: Anticipating unrest in the east, Baozhen saw that Ze and Lu lay on the main troop routes. War had just ended; taxes were crushing and the armies depleted. He registered households and drafted one man from every three, exempting them from corvée and land tax while issuing bows and arrows. In off months the men trained in archery in groups; at year's end he personally inspected the rolls, grading performance and awarding or punishing accordingly.

sentences.zh: 比三年，皆為精兵，舉所部得成卒二萬，既不稟於官，而府庫實。

translations.literal: Within about three years, all became elite troops. Throughout his command he obtained twenty thousand mature soldiers. They were no longer dependent on official supplies, yet the treasury was full.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years they were all crack troops; his command fielded twenty thousand fully trained soldiers at no cost to the central government, while his own treasury grew full.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「軍可用矣。

translations.literal: He then said: "The army can be used."
translations.idiomatic: He declared: "The army is ready."

sentences.zh: 」繕甲淬兵，遂雄山東，天下稱昭義步兵為諸軍冠。

translations.literal: He repaired armor and sharpened weapons, then dominated Shandong. All under heaven called the Zhaoyi infantry the finest of all armies.
translations.idiomatic: He outfitted and honed his forces until they dominated the east; throughout the empire the Zhaoyi infantry were regarded as the finest foot soldiers in any army.

sentences.zh: 久之，為澤潞節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: After some time, he became Campaigning Adjutant of the Ze-Lu Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made campaigning adjutant of the Ze-Lu command.

sentences.zh: 會昭義節度李承昭病，詔抱真權磁邢兵馬留後。

translations.literal: When Zhaoyi Military Governor Li Chengzhao fell ill, an edict had Baozhen act as Acting Military Commissioner for the Ci and Xing troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chengzhao, military governor of Zhaoyi, fell ill, Baozhen was ordered to serve as acting commander of the Ci and Xing forces.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，檢校工部尚書，領昭義節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong succeeded, he was made acting Minister of Works and put in charge of the Zhaoyi Military Governorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Baozhen was made acting Minister of Works and full military governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 建中中，田悅反，圍邢及臨洺，詔抱真與河東馬燧合神策兵救之，敗悅於雙岡，斬其將楊朝光，又破之臨洺，遂解臨洺、邢之圍。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era, Tian Yue rebelled and besieged Xing and Linming. An edict ordered Baozhen and Ma Sui of Hedong to combine Shence troops to rescue them. They defeated Yue at Shuanggang, beheaded his general Yang Chaoguang, and again defeated him at Linming, thus lifting the sieges of Linming and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianzhong, Tian Yue rebelled and besieged Xing and Linming. Baozhen was ordered to join Ma Sui of Hedong and Shence Army troops in relief. They routed Tian Yue at Shuanggang, beheaded his general Yang Chaoguang, defeated him again at Linming, and lifted both sieges.

sentences.zh: 以功檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For these achievements he was made acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 復與悅戰洹水，走之。

translations.literal: Again he fought Yue at Huanshui and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Tian Yue again on the Huanshui River and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 進圍魏，悅戰城下，大敗。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Wei. Yue fought beneath the walls and was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the siege of Weizhou; Tian Yue fought under the walls and suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 進檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會硃滔、王武俊反，救悅，抱真退保魏。

translations.literal: When Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun rebelled to rescue Yue, Baozhen withdrew to hold Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun rebelled to rescue Tian Yue, and Baozhen fell back to defend Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝蒼卒狩奉天，聞問，諸將皆哭，各引麾下還屯。

translations.literal: The Emperor in haste fled to Fengtian. When the news arrived, all the generals wept. Each led his followers back to encamp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled in disarray to Fengtian. When word reached them, the generals wept and each withdrew his forces to their posts.

sentences.zh: 于時，李希烈陷汴，李納反鄆，李懷光相次反河中，抱真獨以數州截然橫絕潰叛中，離沮其奸，為群盜所憚。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xilie captured Bian, Li Na rebelled at Yan, and Li Huaiguang in succession rebelled at Hezhong. Baozhen alone with several prefectures stood sharply athwart the midst of collapse and rebellion, disrupting and discouraging their treachery, and was feared by the band of rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie had taken Bian, Li Na rebelled in Yan, and Li Huaiguang rose in Hezhong in turn. Baozhen alone held several prefectures like a barrier amid the rebellion, sowing division among the rebels and inspiring fear in them all.

sentences.zh: 興元初，檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事，繇倪國公進義陽郡王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan, he was acting Left Vice Director and Chief Councillor, advancing from Duke of Niguo to Prince of Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan he was made acting Left Vice Director and Chief Councillor, advancing from Duke of Niguo to Prince of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 硃滔悉幽薊兵與回紇圍貝州，以應硃泚。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao mustered all You and Ji troops with the Uyghurs to besiege Beizhou, to respond to Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao massed the armies of You and Ji with Uyghur allies to besiege Beizhou in support of Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 而希烈既竊名號，則欲臣制諸叛，眾稍離。

translations.literal: But Xilie having usurped title, then wished to subject and control the various rebels, and the masses gradually split away.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Xilie had declared himself emperor, he tried to bring the other rebel leaders under his command, and their followers began to drift apart.

sentences.zh: 天子下罪己詔，並赦群盜。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued an edict blaming himself and pardoned all the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a self-reproach edict and granted amnesty to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 抱真乃遣客賈林以大義說武俊，使合從擊滔，武俊許諾，而內猶豫。

translations.literal: Baozhen then sent his guest Jia Lin to persuade Wujun with great righteousness, making him join in alliance to strike Tao. Wujun promised, but inwardly hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen sent his retainer Jia Lin to argue the larger cause with Wang Wujun and win him into an alliance against Zhu Tao. Wang Wujun agreed publicly but remained inwardly uncertain.

sentences.zh: 抱真將自造其壁，諉軍事于司馬盧玄卿曰：「吾此行，系時安危，使遂不還，部勒以聽天子命，惟子；

translations.literal: Baozhen was about to go in person to his camp. He entrusted military affairs to his adjutant Lu Xuanqing, saying: "This journey of mine bears on the safety of the times. If I indeed do not return, deploy and obey the Son of Heaven's command—only you;
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen prepared to visit Wang Wujun in person. He entrusted military affairs to his chief of staff Lu Xuanqing: "My journey concerns the fate of the realm. If I do not return, hold the army together and obey the emperor's orders—you alone;

sentences.zh: 勵兵東向，雪吾之恥，亦唯子。

translations.literal: Rouse troops eastward and wipe away my shame—this too is only you."
translations.idiomatic: to march east, restore our honor, and avenge this humiliation—that will also fall to you alone."

sentences.zh: 」即以數騎馳入見武俊，曰：「泚、希烈爭竊帝號，滔攻貝州，此其志皆欲自肆於天下。

translations.literal: With just a few horsemen he galloped in to see Wujun and said: "Ci and Xilie contend in usurping imperial titles. Tao attacks Beizhou. Their intent is all to indulge themselves throughout the empire."
translations.idiomatic: He rode in with only a handful of escorts to see Wang Wujun and said: "Zhu Ci and Li Xilie vie for imperial titles, and Zhu Tao is attacking Beizhou—they all mean to carve up the empire for themselves."

sentences.zh: 足下既不能與競長雄，舍九葉天子而臣反虜乎？

translations.literal: Under your feet, if you cannot compete for supremacy, will you abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and serve the rebel barbarians?"
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot compete with them for supremacy, will you forsake an emperor of nine generations and submit to a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 且詔書罪己，禹、湯之心也。

translations.literal: Moreover the edict blaming himself—this is the heart of Yu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, an edict of self-reproach is the spirit of Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 方上暴露播越，公能自安乎？

translations.literal: Just now the sovereign is exposed and driven about in exile. Can you, sir, be at ease?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor is wandering in hardship and exile—can you truly rest at ease?"

sentences.zh: 」因持武俊，涕下交頤，武俊亦感泣，左右皆泣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he grasped Wujun. Tears streamed down both cheeks. Wujun also wept in moved response. Those to left and right all wept.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Wang Wujun's hands, tears streaming down his face. Wang Wujun wept in turn, and everyone present wept.

sentences.zh: 退臥帳中，甘寢久之。

translations.literal: He withdrew and lay in the tent, sleeping sweetly for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to the tent and slept soundly for a long while.

sentences.zh: 武俊感其不疑，乃益恭，指心誓天曰：「此身已許公死矣！

translations.literal: Wujun, moved that he had no suspicion, became all the more respectful. Pointing to his heart he swore to Heaven: "This body is already pledged to die for you, sir!"
translations.idiomatic: Moved by Baozhen's trust, Wang Wujun became still more deferential. Pointing to his heart he swore: "This life is already yours!"

sentences.zh: 」食訖，約為昆弟而別。

translations.literal: When the meal was finished, they pledged to be brothers and parted.
translations.idiomatic: After the meal they swore brotherhood and parted.

sentences.zh: 旦日合戰，大破滔經城。

translations.literal: The next day they joined battle and greatly defeated Tao at Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they joined battle and routed Zhu Tao at Jingcheng.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司空，實封六百戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Grand Master of Works with a fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Grand Master of Works with an enfeoffment of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，朝京師，詔還所鎮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, he attended court at the capital. An edict sent him back to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign he went to court and was then ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 抱真喜士，聞世賢者，必欲與之遊，雖小善，皆卑禮厚幣數千里邀致之，至無可錄，徐徐以禮謝。

translations.literal: Baozhen delighted in scholars. Hearing of worthy men of the age, he always wished to associate with them. Even for small talents, all received humble courtesy and generous gifts, invited from thousands of li. When there was nothing worth recording, he slowly dismissed them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen loved men of talent. Whenever he heard of a worthy man he sought his company, sending humble invitations and rich gifts across hundreds of miles even for modest talents. When a guest proved unworthy, he politely dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 會天下稍無事，乃飾台沼以自娛。

translations.literal: When the realm was somewhat without affairs, he then adorned terraces and ponds for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm grew relatively peaceful, he landscaped terraces and ponds for his own enjoyment.

sentences.zh: 好方士，謂不死可致。

translations.literal: He favored alchemical masters and believed immortality could be attained.
translations.idiomatic: He patronized Daoist alchemists, believing that immortality could be achieved.

sentences.zh: 有孫季長者為治丹，且曰：「服此當仙去。

translations.literal: There was one Sun Jichang who prepared elixir for him, saying: "If you take this you shall depart as an immortal."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Sun Jichang prepared elixirs for him, saying, "Take this and you will ascend as an immortal."

sentences.zh: 」抱真表署幕府。

translations.literal: Baozhen memorialized to appoint him to the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen had him appointed to his staff by imperial memorial.

sentences.zh: 嘗語左右曰：「秦、漢君不偶此，我乃得之，後升天，不復見公等矣。

translations.literal: He once told those around him: "Emperors of Qin and Han did not chance upon this. I have obtained it. Later when I ascend to heaven, I shall not see you gentlemen again."
translations.idiomatic: He told his attendants: "The emperors of Qin and Han never had this chance—I have found it. When I ascend to heaven, I shall not see you again."

sentences.zh: 」夜夢駕鶴，寤而刻寓鶴，衣羽服，習乘之。

translations.literal: At night he dreamed of riding a crane. Waking, he carved a dwelling crane, wore feather robes, and practiced riding it.
translations.idiomatic: He dreamed one night that he was riding a crane. On waking he had a wooden crane carved, donned feather robes, and practiced mounting it.

sentences.zh: 後益惑厭勝，因疾，請降官，七讓司空，還為左僕射。

translations.literal: Later he became increasingly deluded with exorcistic rituals. Because of illness he requested reduction of rank. Seven times he declined Grand Master of Works and returned to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He grew ever more obsessed with occult rites. When illness struck he petitioned to be demoted, declining the Grand Master of Works seven times until he was restored to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 餌丹二萬丸，不能食，且死，醫以彘肪穀漆下之。

translations.literal: He ingested twenty thousand pills of elixir, could not eat, and was near death. A physician used pig fat and grain lacquer to purge it downward.
translations.idiomatic: After swallowing twenty thousand elixir pills he could no longer eat and was near death; physicians purged the poison with pig fat and lacquer.

sentences.zh: 疾少間，季長曰：「危得仙，何自棄也？

translations.literal: When the illness eased slightly, Jichang said: "You were nearly immortal—why abandon it?"
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered somewhat, Sun Jichang said: "You were on the verge of immortality—why give up now?"

sentences.zh: 」益服三千丸，卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: He further ingested three thousand pills and died, age sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He took three thousand more pills and died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 抱真子 緘其子殿中侍御史緘匿喪，與其屬盧會昌元仲經謀，會諸將，仲經詭抱真令曰：「吾疾不任事，令緘典軍，勉佐之。

translations.literal: Baozhen's son Jian. His son, Palace Censor Jian, concealed the death. With his subordinate Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he plotted, assembled the generals, and Zhongjing falsely issued Baozhen's order: "My illness does not allow me to handle affairs. I order Jian to command the army—assist him diligently."
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen's son Jian, a palace censor, concealed his father's death. With his aide Lu Huichang and Yuan Zhongjing he summoned the generals, and Zhongjing forged orders in Baozhen's name: "I am too ill to command. Jian will take charge of the army—support him faithfully."

sentences.zh: 」副使李說及諸校俯首，皆嘸曰；

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Li Shuo and the various officers bowed their heads. All murmured assent:
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Li Shuo and the other officers bowed low and murmured their assent:

translations.literal: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」緘盛服出，眾拜之，悉發府庫勞軍。

translations.literal: Jian came out in full dress. The assembly bowed to him. All the treasury stores were opened to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jian appeared in full regalia; the officers bowed to him and the treasury was emptied to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 會昌即為抱真表，翌日，令諸將署章，請以節付緘。

translations.literal: Huichang immediately submitted a memorial for Baozhen. The next day he had the generals sign a petition asking that the command baton be given to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huichang at once submitted a memorial in Baozhen's name, and the next day had the generals sign a petition requesting that military authority pass to Jian.

sentences.zh: 天子已聞抱真喪，遣使者馳入軍，詔以事屬大將王延貴。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven had already heard of Baozhen's death and dispatched an envoy galloping into the army, decreeing that affairs be entrusted to the great general Wang Yangui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already learned of Baozhen's death and sent an envoy posthaste to the army, ordering that command devolve upon General Wang Yangui.

sentences.zh: 緘謾若抱真疾，請詰朝見，凡三日，緘乃出見使者，陳兵甚嚴。

translations.literal: Jian pretended as if Baozhen were ill and requested to meet the envoy the next morning. For three days he delayed. Jian then came out to meet the envoy, arrayed troops very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Jian feigned that Baozhen was merely ill and asked to defer the audience until the next day—then kept the envoy waiting three days before appearing with a heavily armed escort.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「朝廷已知公薨，詔以兵屬延貴，君速歸發喪。

translations.literal: The envoy said: "The court already knows the lord has died. The decree assigns the troops to Yangui. My lord, quickly return and hold the funeral."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said: "The court knows your father is dead. The edict assigns the army to Wang Yangui—you must return at once and hold the funeral."

sentences.zh: 」緘愕然，謂諸將曰：「詔不許，若何？

translations.literal: Jian was startled. He said to the generals: "The decree does not permit it—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian was stunned. He asked the officers: "The edict refuses us—what then?"

sentences.zh: 」眾不對。

translations.literal: The assembly did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 乃遽以印鑰上監軍，始發喪。

translations.literal: He then hurriedly surrendered the seal and keys to the army supervisor and only then held the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He hastily surrendered the seal and keys to the army supervisor and only then announced the death.

sentences.zh: 使者趣延貴視事，護緘赴東都，仲經逃諸外，捕殺之，會昌得不坐。

translations.literal: The envoy urged Yangui to assume office, escorted Jian to the Eastern Capital. Zhongjing fled outside and was captured and killed. Huichang was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy installed Wang Yangui and escorted Jian to the Eastern Capital. Zhongjing fled but was hunted down and executed; Lu Huichang escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 始，緘遣將陳榮以書抵武俊，假其財。

translations.literal: Initially, Jian sent his general Chen Rong with a letter to Wujun to borrow his funds.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jian had sent General Chen Rong to Wang Wujun with a letter requesting a loan.

sentences.zh: 武俊怒曰；

translations.literal: Wujun angrily said:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wujun angrily replied:

sentences.zh: 「吾與乃公善者，恭王命，非同惡也。

translations.literal: "My friendship with your father was in respect of the king's command—not shared evil."
translations.idiomatic: "Your father and I stood together out of loyalty to the throne—not because we were partners in crime."

sentences.zh: 今聞已亡，誰詐其子使不俟朝制邪？

translations.literal: Now I hear he is already dead. Who deceived his son to make him not await the court's ordinance?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear he is dead—who tricked his son into seizing command before the court could act?"

sentences.zh: 」囚榮而讓緘焉。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Rong and reproached Jian for it.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Chen Rong and rebuked Jian through him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈抱真太保。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded Baozhen Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored Baozhen as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 路嗣恭路嗣恭，字懿範，京兆三原人，始名劍客，以世廕為鄴尉。

translations.literal: Lu Sigong—Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao. His original name was Jianké. Through hereditary privilege he became magistrate of Ye District.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sigong, courtesy name Yifan, was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao. His original name was Jianké. He entered office through hereditary privilege as magistrate of Ye District.

sentences.zh: 席豫黜陟河朔，表為蕭關令，連徙神烏、姑臧二縣，考績為天下最。

translations.literal: When Xi Yu was managing promotions and demotions in Hebei, he recommended [Sigong] as magistrate of Xiaoguan; [Sigong] was successively transferred through the two counties Shenwu and Guzang; his merit evaluation was the highest in the empire.
translations.idiomatic: While Xi Yu oversaw personnel decisions in Hebei, he recommended Lu Sigong for magistrate of Xiaoguan. Lu Sigong was then transferred in succession to Shenwu and Guzang, and his performance reviews ranked highest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以為可嗣漢魯恭，因賜名。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong considered him able to succeed Han's Lu Gong, and therefore bestowed the name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong believed he could follow in the footsteps of Lu Gong of Han, that paragon of virtuous rule, and bestowed on him a new name.

sentences.zh: 轉渭南令，主杜化、東陽二驛。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Weinan magistrate, overseeing the two relay stations Duhao and Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Weinan, with charge of the Duhao and Dongyang relay stations.

sentences.zh: 時關畿用兵，使人系道，嗣恭儲具有素，而民不擾。

translations.literal: At the time the capital region was at war; messengers filled the roads. Sigong had long prepared stores and supplies, and the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital region was at war and couriers clogged every road, Sigong's thorough preparations kept the populace from hardship.

sentences.zh: 後為郭子儀朔方節度留後，大將孫守亮擁重兵，驕蹇不受制，嗣恭因稱疾，守亮至，即殺之，一軍皆震。

translations.literal: Later he served as acting chief of staff under Guo Ziyi's Shuofang military governorship. The great general Sun Shouliang held heavy troops, was arrogant and obstinate, and refused control. Sigong feigned illness; when Shouliang arrived, he immediately killed him, and the whole army was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as acting chief of staff under Guo Ziyi's Shuofang command, he faced General Sun Shouliang, who controlled a large force, grew insubordinate, and refused orders. Sigong pretended to be ill; when Shouliang came to visit, Sigong killed him on the spot, and the entire army was stunned.

sentences.zh: 永泰三年，檢校刑部尚書，知省事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongtai, [he was] acting Minister of Justice, directing Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 766, the third year of Yongtai, he was appointed acting Minister of Justice and put in charge of Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 出為江西觀察使，以善治財賦稱。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Jiangxi observation commissioner, famed for skill in managing finances and levies.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Jiangxi observation commissioner and won renown for his skill in managing revenue and taxation.

sentences.zh: 有賈明觀者，素事魚朝恩，朝恩誅，當坐死，宰相元載納其賂，遣效力江西，將行，居民數萬懷瓦石候擊，載諭市吏禁止，乃得去。

translations.literal: There was one Jia Mingguan who had long served Yu Chaoen. When Chaoen was executed he should have been condemned to death, but Chief Minister Yuan Zai accepted his bribe and sent him to serve in Jiangxi to redeem himself through merit. As he was about to depart, tens of thousands of residents waited with tiles and stones to ambush and strike him. Zai ordered market officials to forbid it, and only then was he able to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mingguan had long served Yu Chaoen; when Chaoen was executed, Mingguan deserved death, but Chief Minister Yuan Zai took his bribe and sent him to Jiangxi to earn redemption through service. As he prepared to leave, tens of thousands of townspeople gathered with tiles and stones to stone him. Only when Zai ordered the market officers to stop them could Mingguan get away.

sentences.zh: 魏少游畏載，常回容之，及嗣恭代少遊，即日杖死。

translations.literal: Wei Shaoyou feared Zai and always indulgently accommodated him; when Sigong replaced Shaoyou, he had him beaten to death the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaoyou, who feared Yuan Zai, had long protected Mingguan; when Sigong replaced Shaoyou, he had Mingguan flogged to death that very day.

sentences.zh: 大曆八年，嶺南將哥舒晃殺節度使呂崇賁，五嶺大擾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dali, the Lingnan general Geshu Huang killed the military governor Lü Chongbin, and the Five Ridges were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In 773, the eighth year of Dali, Lingnan general Geshu Huang murdered military governor Lü Chongbin, throwing the Five Ridges into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 詔嗣恭兼嶺南節度使，封冀國公。

translations.literal: An edict made Sigong concurrently Lingnan military governor and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Sigong concurrently as Lingnan military governor and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 嗣恭募勇敢士八千人，以流人孟瑤、敬冕為才，擢任之。

translations.literal: Sigong recruited eight thousand bold warriors; deeming the exiles Meng Yao and Jing Mian talented, he promoted and employed them.
translations.idiomatic: Sigong raised eight thousand bold fighters and, recognizing talent in the banished men Meng Yao and Jing Mian, promoted them to command.

sentences.zh: 使瑤督大軍當其沖，冕率輕兵由間道出不意，遂斬晃及支党萬餘，築屍為京觀。

translations.literal: He had Yao command the main army to meet the enemy head-on; Mian led light troops by a hidden path to strike unexpectedly. They then beheaded Huang and more than ten thousand of his faction and built the corpses into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yao took the main force straight at the enemy; Jing Mian led light troops by a side path for a surprise attack. They cut down Huang and more than ten thousand of his followers and heaped the dead into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 俚洞魁宿為惡者，皆族夷之。

translations.literal: The chieftains of the Li cave settlements who had long been evil were all exterminated, clan and all.
translations.idiomatic: Li chieftains who had long terrorized the region were executed to the last of their clans.

sentences.zh: 還為檢校兵部尚書，復知省事。

translations.literal: He returned as acting Minister of War and again directed Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as acting Minister of War and again handled Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 嗣恭起州縣吏，以課治進至顯官，及晃事株戮舶商，沒其財數百萬私有之，代宗惡焉，故賞不酬功。

translations.literal: Sigong had risen from county and district clerk, advancing through administrative merit to eminent office; but in the Huang affair he executed wholesale the merchant ship owners and confiscated their wealth—millions—for his private use. Emperor Daizong detested this, and therefore rewards did not match his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Sigong had worked his way up from a local clerk to high office through outstanding administration, but after defeating Huang he massacred merchant ship owners and seized millions in goods for himself. Emperor Daizong was disgusted, and Sigong's rewards never matched his achievements.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，陰賕宰相楊炎，炎錄前效，更拜兵部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: When Dezong ascended, [Sigong] secretly bribed Chief Minister Yang Yan; Yan recorded his past service and had him reappointed Minister of War and Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong came to the throne, Sigong secretly bribed Chief Minister Yang Yan, who cited his past service and had him appointed Minister of War and Protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 俄加懷鄭汝陝河陽三城節度、東都畿觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made military governor of the Three Cities of Huai, Zheng, Ru, Shaan, and Heyang, and observation commissioner of the eastern capital capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given additional commands as military governor of Huai, Zheng, Ru, Shaan, and Heyang, and as observation commissioner of the eastern capital region.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one; posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously honored as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 子應、恕。

translations.literal: His sons were Ying and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Ying and Shu.

sentences.zh: 子 應應，字從眾，以廕為著作郎。

translations.literal: His son Ying—Ying, courtesy name Congzhong—entered office through hereditary privilege as Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying, courtesy name Congzhong, entered office by inheritance as Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，出為虔州刺史，詔嗣父封。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenyuan era he was sent out as prefect of Ganzhou; an edict allowed him to inherit his father's enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan reign he was posted prefect of Ganzhou, with an edict permitting him to succeed to his father's noble rank.

sentences.zh: 鑿贛石梗嶮以通舟道。

translations.literal: He cut through the obstructing, perilous rocks of Ganshi to open the channel for boats.
translations.idiomatic: He blasted away the treacherous rock obstructions at Ganshi to open the river to navigation.

sentences.zh: 德宗時，李泌為相，號得君。

translations.literal: During the Dezong era, Li Bi served as chief minister and was reputed to have gained the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, Li Bi served as chief minister and enjoyed the emperor's full trust.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「誰於卿有恩者，朕能報之。

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "Is there anyone who has shown you kindness? I can repay them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked him, "Tell me who has been kind to you—I will see them rewarded."
